parsed.explanation: The combined national and state/province regime creates real traveller-facing exposure: sex-assigned-at-birth document rules, border refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document/sex doubts, facility bans with criminal trespass in some states, care-funding bans covering adults and minors in this state/province, and documented abuse in immigration and correctional custody. National litigation, existing X passports, private care, and the national hate-crime statute are partial mitigants. There is no general death penalty or routine imprisonment for trans identity, but outing at a border or in a restricted facility can lead to refusal, detention, male placement, or prosecution. This sits in the High Risk band, below jurisdictions where exclusion is administrative only and above those with routine arrest and lethal custody.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned-at-birth markers, stop new X markers, and border cable directs refusal or added evidence where documents or sex are doubted; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud ineligibility. Athlete entry ban exists.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements with limited waiver; litigation and legal-aid FAQ exist.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport or presentation mismatch can trigger secondary inspection and onward immigration fraud/removal exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections adopt conversion-style practices, hormone removal, and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute exists; no documented custody protection or consular remedy in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document doubt can move a traveller into immigration detention; custody placement and treatment then compound.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans cover many states; this state/province bans K-12 and state-owned facility use by birth sex; four states criminalise certain bathroom use; a trans student was arrested and held 24 hours in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states and cities have no ban or have protections; national hate-crime law exists; no state gender-identity accommodation law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Adult or family using a government-building restroom or changing room risks refusal, ejection, trespass charge, or male custody.

care_services.exposure: State/province SB 904 bars public funds, state Medicaid, and state-owned facilities for gender-affirming care for minors and adults; intentional employee violations are misdemeanors; national rules restrict minors' coverage.
care_services.protection: Private facilities, private insurance, and out-of-pocket care remain; emergency and specified exempt care remain; national legal challenges continue.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care in a public facility may be denied; private care is possible but costly; a minor with a guardian is especially affected.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders label gender ideology, direct school investigations and prosecution over social transition, and a counterterrorism strategy names radically pro-transgender groups; state executive order defines sex for all state purposes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders are enjoined or blocked; the counterterrorism document says powers will not target mere disagreement; litigation is unresolved.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official suspicion of visible trans identity or advocacy is raised and reporting chilled, though direct visitor prosecution is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: State/province school-facility ban and care-funding/facility ban cover minors; national order threatens teachers over preferred names and pronouns; the K-12 bathroom law is linked to a resident student's death.
minors_guardians.protection: Private care remains; some court blocks exist; emergency exemptions apply.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces facility exclusion and care denial; a guardian may face investigation if school social transition is involved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity; documented threats against a trans student and a fatal beating of a nonbinary student exist; no visitor-specific violence is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some city nondiscrimination ordinances and a national employment ruling exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is uneven; visitors lack local networks; national prosecution is available but not shown operating for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The state/province has no gender-identity antidiscrimination statute, at-will employment, a state supreme court that foreclosed birth-certificate corrections, and stopped custody reporting.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation and injunctions, a legal-aid FAQ, the national hate-crime statute, and some city ordinances exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are contested and slow nationally; state-level recourse for facilities and care is absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra uses border registration to exclude and humiliate but documents no arrest or custody harm. This dossier is lower: it adds possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, facility trespass, care bans, and documented immigration-custody abuse.

Kestrel Isles uses secondary screening and administrative refusal with appeal desks. This dossier is lower: border doubt can feed fraud findings, facilities can trigger criminal trespass, and custody harms are documented.

Meridia has trained border officers, tribunal review, and brief detention ending in release. This dossier is much lower: it has hostile national framing, no effective border remedy shown, facility exclusion, and severe custody reports.

Varnalia shows raids, fines, and detention but imprisonment is rare and execution is not imposed. This dossier is broadly similar in severity, though its exposures are more national-entry and custody-based than street-raid-based.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national entry and custody policy layered onto a restrictive state/province. The sharpest traveller exposures are document/sex mismatch at the border, possible fraud ineligibility, facility exclusion or trespass, care denial in public facilities, and severe treatment if detained. State law adds no gender-identity accommodation or hate-crime protection, while national litigation, existing X passports, private care, and the national hate-crime statute provide only partial and contested mitigation. Outing can produce refusal, detention, male placement, or prosecution; execution is not a credible general outcome.
